A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical experiments on synthetic distributions and KL-estimation results using Gemma 2 9B IT on four Alpaca prompts (Figure 4; Appendix C).

after.justification: v3 retains those results and adds negative-length-reward experiments, estimator-dispersion results, and German/French translation examples (Figures 3, 5, 10–11).

M1.justification: The best-of-n, rewind-and-repeat, and blockwise sampling procedures and proposed KL-estimator formula remain unchanged. Renaming d to d_n and evaluating another reward function do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds four translation prompts: a short sentence and the paper's abstract translated into German and French. This provides limited task and language expansion beyond the retained synthetic examples and four Alpaca prompts.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparison methods, including the analytical KL formula, alternative bounds, and win-rate-optimal and rewind-and-repeat policies. Added experiments reuse existing estimators; Figure 3's tilted curves describe variability rather than new comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluations using negative response length as reward alongside log-likelihood reward (Figures 5 and 11). The retained Alpaca experiment's Gemma model, temperature-one setting, and 100-sample upper-bound procedure are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds reward-sensitivity checks using negative length and examines estimator dispersion on the existing nonuniform synthetic examples. The underlying examples and their expected-value analyses were already present in v2.

E5.justification: v2 reports expected estimator curves and acknowledges variance. v3 adds tilted min/max dispersion curves, their computation in Appendix C.2, and variance/sample-averaging discussion. These summaries are not calibrated confidence intervals, and no explicit increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Original result curves are retained. New results cover negative-length reward, translation, and estimator dispersion. Figure 10 shows estimates saturating below the analytical formula for short translations but nearly coinciding with it for abstract translations; Figure 3 reveals substantial spread in some rare-outcome regimes.

T1.justification: v3 adds Lemma 4.5, bounding every estimator realization between zero and the analytical KL formula, with a proof in Appendix A.2. It also introduces the tilted-average definition and limiting properties in Appendix C.2. Existing principal bounds, assumptions, and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The principal KL, estimator, and win-rate claims remain. The conclusion qualifies the comparison with rewind-and-repeat by acknowledging its advantage for increasing reward under a fixed compute budget. Test-time compute scaling is also foregrounded in the abstract.

C2.justification: v3 explains high estimator variability through the appearance of rare outcomes and discusses the unresolved compute–reward–KL tradeoff. Its Impact Statement replaces generic text with specific capability-preservation and adversarial-jailbreaking implications.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds exact translation prompts and the t=-1 and t=1 choices for tilted summaries. Randomized checks of Conjecture 4.4 are newly described as tens of thousands of cases, without establishing an increase. Existing Alpaca implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Beetham et al. (2024), Korbak et al. (2022a), and Li et al. (2023), and expands discussion of already-cited Mroueh. Publication updates for retained works such as Amini and Sessa do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introduction and conclusion expansions, a rewritten Impact Statement, revised heading capitalization, and subdivision of Appendix C into three subsections. The main narrative sequence and appendix proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental graphics expand substantially through three new four-panel figures: Figure 5 and Appendix Figures 10–11. Figure 3 gains tilted min/max curves and an expanded legend. Retained figures are otherwise relocated or renumbered, with their original curves preserved.

improvement.justification: The added experiments, Lemma 4.5 and its proof, and compute-budget qualification improve coverage and characterization. However, Section 4 newly claims that M=O(log n log(1/delta)) independent draws guarantee standard deviation below delta; averaging reduces standard deviation as 1/sqrt(M), so that guarantee does not follow. Useful additions coexist with a mathematical error in the new uncertainty discussion, leaving the net quality improvement unclear.
